children: WINNIPEG, Manitoba--Intercontinental Exchange canola futures were weaker at mid-session Monday, falling back by double digits.
"Canola is subject to profit-taking and the impending harvest," an analyst said, noting the speculative funds still hold a very large long position in the Canadian oilseed.
Alberta reported Friday that in its south the canola harvest was nearly 1% complete.
Pressure on canola also was coming from declines in the Chicago soy complex. European rapeseed was lower as well and the Malaysian palm oil market was closed for a holiday.
Crude oil swung higher following the exchange of attacks between the U.S. and Iran. However, the spillover was doing little to alleviate the losses in the vegetable oils.
Despite Monday's losses, the November canola contract was still holding above its major moving averages.
Pakistan is back buying Canadian canola after ceasing its purchases from 2023 to 2025. So far in 2026, Pakistan has imported almost 506,700 tonnes.
The Canadian dollar was higher with the loonie at 72.14 U.S. cents late Monday morning, compared with Friday's close of 72.00.
About 36,800 canola contracts were traded as of 11:36 a.m. ET with prices in Canadian dollars per metric tonne:
